docs.text: Running log of what changed in anycalc and why. Newest entries at the bottom (append to note maks it at the bottom). Format: date — change — reason. 2026-10-23 — requirements.txt → pyproject.toml; Linux build verified from the workspace root requirements.txt is gone ; there is now a pyproject.toml at the workspace root. [project].dependencies = flet[cli,desktop]>=1.0.4 + PyYAML>=6.0.3 (identical pins/extras to the final requirements.txt, comments carried over), dev tooling moved to [project.optional-dependencies].dev ( pytest , pytest-asyncio ) so it stays out of a runtime install, requires-python = ">=3.11" , [build-system] = setuptools. The entry point is declared inside **src/** in two places on purpose: [tool.flet.app] path = "src" + module = "main" (used by flet run / flet build ) and [project.scripts] anycalc = "src.main:run_app" (installed by pip install -e . ). Supporting pieces: new src/__init__.py , [tool.setuptools] packages = ["src"] , [tool.setuptools.package-data] src = ["assets/*.yaml"] so conversions.yaml travels with an installed distribution. src/main.py no longer ends in a bare module-level ft.run(main) ; it now defines def run_app(): ft.run(main) behind if __name__ == "__main__": run_app() . That closes the old "importing main.py launches the app" obstacle for tests, and it is safe in packaged builds because a Flet bundle executes the configured app module as ___main___ ( _sp_run_module_as_main() in the generated build/flutter/lib/python.dart : "Execute the configured app module as the real __main__ module") rather than importing it. Flet packaging metadata moved in too: [tool.flet] org = "com.<personal>" — an id derived from a personal name, since scrubbed out of every commit by the 2026-10-24 PII sweep below — product = "anycalc" , [tool.flet.linux] categories = ["Utility"] → the bundle's app id / launcher name was <org>.anycalc / anycalc . Build test run from the workspace root, not from **src/** : .venv/bin/flet build linux --no-rich-output --yes → "Successfully built your app for Linux!" in ~2.5 min. That works only because [tool.flet.app] points the CLI at src/main.py ; run from src/ it would look for a pyproject.toml there and find none. validate_entry_point() ( flet_cli/commands/build_base.py:992 ) is what errors with "main.py not found in the root of Flet app directory" when app.path / app.module are wrong. Artifact: build/linux/ (132 MB) = native GTK runner anycalc (embeds CPython 3.14 via libpython3.14.so ), app/ with main.pyc + __init__.pyc (the app is compiled by default ; --no-compile-app keeps sources) and app/assets/conversions.yaml — sha256 identical to the source file, site-packages/ installed from pyproject (resolved flet 1.0.5 + flet-cli + flet-desktop + PyYAML), data/flutter_assets , share/applications/<org>.anycalc.desktop . build/flutter (439 MB) is the intermediate Flutter project; total build/ ≈ 625 MB. Smoke test of the artifact: WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0 XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 ./build/linux/anycalc stayed alive for the full 15 s until timeout killed it (exit 124) with only the harmless Gdk-Message: Unable to load from the cursor theme — no traceback, so the packaged entry point booted. Confirmed independently by unmarshalling app/main.pyc with the bundled-stdlib version: it contains both main and run_app and the __main__ guard. Packaging check without touching .venv : pip wheel . --no-deps produced anycalc-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl containing src/main.py , src/__init__.py , src/assets/conversions.yaml and entry_points.txt ( anycalc = src.main:run_app ). Gotcha: .venv has no setuptools , so --no-build-isolation fails there — pip's build isolation (i.e. network) is required to build this project. Flutter for the build: Flet 1.0.4 pins Flutter 3.44.8 ( flet/version.py ); find_flutter_batch() prefers the managed SDK at ~/flutter/3.44.8 before falling back to PATH , and that copy already exists on this machine, so no download/prompt was needed ( --yes was passed anyway). cmake / ninja / pkg-config / gcc are present. Docs touched: README.md filled in (setup, run, build — it was empty), AGENTS.md rule now says keep pyproject.toml updated. 2026-10-23 — requirements.txt made complete (runtime deps only) Was flet>=1.0.4 + PyYAML>=6.0.3 ; now flet[cli,desktop]>=1.0.4 + PyYAML>=6.0.3 , each with a comment saying what it is for. Reason: in Flet 1.x the desktop runtime is an extra , not a dependency. Plain flet pulls only httpx , msgpack , oauthlib , repath ; ft.run() then calls ensure_flet_desktop_package_installed() ( flet/app.py:305 → flet/utils/pip.py:88 ), which pip-installs flet-desktop behind your back on first launch. Declaring the extra keeps a fresh install deterministic and offline-safe, and Flet pins its extras to its own exact version, so the bracket group can never drift from the SDK. [cli] is included because the app is launched with flet run . [web] is deliberately not included (it would drag in fastapi / uvicorn / websockets for a target this desktop app does not ship). [test] (pytest, pytest-asyncio, numpy, pillow, scikit-image) is dev tooling and stays out. Audited every import in src/ (re-checked during the pyproject migration): everything else is stdlib ( ast , asyncio , math , operator , collections , dataclasses , decimal , pathlib , typing ), so nothing was missing besides the Flet extras. Transitive deps are left to pip. Verified from scratch: a clean venv built only from requirements.txt resolved flet 1.0.5 + flet-cli / flet-desktop / flet-platform-assets 1.0.5 + PyYAML 6.0.3 , pip check clean, and the full headless UI probe passed in that venv — so the app is good on 1.0.5 too, not just the 1.0.4 in .venv . 2026-10-23 — Live calculation: Convert button removed, live answer under the display Unit conversions no longer have a "Convert" button. run_conversion() is wired to the value field's on_change and to both unit dropdowns' on_select , so the result and the chain of operations refresh the moment the value or a unit changes. A small hint line ("Converts as you type or change units" with a swap icon) took the button's place. Typing noise is silent: an empty value or something that is not a number yet ( - , 3. , abc ) clears the result and the chain without setting a field error; only genuine failures such as having no valid route still surface as result_field.error . The old "Enter a value to convert" error, the "Select both a source and target unit" check and clear_conversion_output() were removed. Both calculators now show a live answer: a small grey ( #9CA3AF , 15 px) number under the expression box that re-evaluates the expression on every change. preview_answer() returns "" for an empty expression, one that cannot be evaluated yet (half-typed), one that is already a single number, or an error message — refresh_preview() hides the slot in those cases. Hooked into every path that can change the expression or what it means: update_display() (keypad, history insert, variable insert), handle_display_change() (typing), toggle_angle() (DEG/RAD), assign_variable() (a new variable value), and set_mode() , which resets the slot. Pressing = does not make that number vanish. promote_preview() grows it to the display size (34), turns it white, slides it up PREVIEW_MORPH_LIFT = 34 px and fades it out over PREVIEW_MORPH_MS = 260 ms using Flet implicit animations ( animate_size / animate_offset / animate_opacity with ft.AnimationStyle(duration=…, curve=ft.AnimationCurve.EASE_OUT_CUBIC) ). The display already holds the answer during the morph, so the two converge instead of anything disappearing. Morph cleanup: page.run_task(finish_preview_morph, token) resets the slot after the animation; the token makes a stale timer a no-op, and the preview_morphing flag keeps refresh_preview() from fighting an animation in flight. All tunables are module constants at the top of main.py . The display panel grew 140 → 168 px for the preview line; asyncio was added to the imports (stdlib, so no dependency change). Verified with a headless Flet drive-through ( /tmp/live_probe.py ): no Convert button in the tree; typing 2500 cm → km gives 0.025 with a 2-hop chain; "-" and "abc" clear silently with no errors; changing From to metre re-converts 5 → 0.005 without touching the value; the same-unit zero-step card still appears. Calculator: preview shows 4 for "2+2" and 25 for "2+23"; after = the display reads 25 while the preview is at 34 px / white / opacity 0 / offset −34 and still visible; ~0.5 s later the slot is hidden again at 15 px, offset 0, opacity 1. Also checked: "sqrt(9" hidden → "sqrt(9)" previews 3, scientific "sin(30)" previews 0.49999999999999994, AC hides it, switching destinations hides it, and 2÷0 previews nothing while the display still reads "Can't divide by 0". Regression: /tmp/chain_probe4.py was updated to the live wiring (it drives value_field.on_change instead of clicking Convert, and now expects a unit change to re-convert rather than clear) and still passes, as does the formula-flip property check /tmp/flip_test.py . Spotted, deliberately not changed: sin(30) in DEG mode evaluates to 0.49999999999999994 rather than 0.5 — a pre-existing precision artifact of the degree conversion that the live preview now makes visible. calculator_spec.md : the conversions section states the live conversion and the silent-while-typing behaviour; "changing a dropdown clears result and chain" became "re-converts the value already in the field"; new "Live result preview" section for the calculators. 2026-10-23 — Chain: formula moved behind a "View formula" button Chain cards now show only the hop ("Centimeter (cm) → Meter (m)") and that hop's values ("2500 → 25"). The inline formula text, the "MD formula applied backwards" note and the chain copy button were all removed. Each card carries a "View formula" button that reveals that hop's formula and collapses it on a second click. For a hop that reused an MD formula backwards the formula is shown already flipped, so what is on screen is always the formula that was actually applied: configured x + 273.15 is shown as x - 273.15 . Reason (user request): the cards were busy — the formula was always visible even when it was not wanted, and announcing "applied backwards" is redundant once the formula itself is presented in the direction it was used. Implementation: _flip_conversion_formula() builds the reversed formula as an AST and unparses it, mirroring the algebra of _invert_conversion_formula() (+ ↔ −, × ↔ ÷). Dividing by a fraction is rewritten as multiplying by its reciprocal, so (x * 9/5) + 32 flips to (x - 32) * 5 / 9 and (x - 32) * 5/9 flips to x * 9 / 5 + 32 . ConversionStep gained applied_formula (the configured text is still kept in formula ); describe_conversion_step() was deleted. Verified two ways: a property check over all 76 MD formulas in conversions.yaml (every flip round-trips numerically through the app's own evaluator and agrees with the numeric solver), and a headless Flet session driving the real UI — formulas hidden until clicked, one button per hop, reveal/hide toggle, flipped formula on a reversed hop, a mixed 3-hop chain (Rankine → Kelvin), zero-step chain with no buttons, chain cleared on unit change, error path intact. Scripts: /tmp/flip_test.py , /tmp/chain_probe4.py . Probe gotcha: a card's title and its value line both contain "→", so matching "→" alone conflates "1. Centimeter (cm) → Meter (m)" with "2500 → 25". Batched shell calls race: launching a probe and reading its output file in the same parallel batch reads the file before the probe writes it. Chain dependent commands with ; in one command string instead. 2026-10-23 — Conversion chain of operations Superseded the same day by the entry above (formula now hidden behind a button, no chain copy). Added a "Chain of operations (N steps)" section under the unit conversion result: one card per formula hop, in the order applied. Each card named the hop by unit name and symbol ("Centimeter (cm) → Meter (m)") and showed the configured formula with that step's input and output ("x / 100 where x = 2500 gives 25"). Reason: the app picks a route through the YAML formula graph automatically, so users could not see how a result was reached, which hop each value passed through, or that a formula had been reused backwards. Hops that reused an MD formula inverted were labelled "MD formula applied backwards"; converting a unit to itself showed a zero-step chain ("the value is passed through unchanged"). convert_units() now returns a ConversionOutcome (value + list of ConversionStep ) instead of a bare Decimal . A step records the hop direction, the formula type, and the value in/out — the hop units are swapped when the formula was inverted. The chain carried its own copy button, reusing the shared clipboard service from the copy-to-clipboard work below. Changing either unit dropdown now clears the previous result and chain, so a result and a chain that do not belong together are never displayed side by side. Verified by driving the real app in a headless Flet session: the drawer handler opened the Length and Temperature forms, Convert was clicked, and the rendered texts were read back out of the control tree. Also asserted the chain text reached the system clipboard. Two real bugs that only the drive-through exposed (a launch check passes both): clear_conversion_output was bound by the dropdowns before its def ran ( UnboundLocalError ), and Flet 1.0.4's Dropdown has no on_change — the event is on_select . 2026-10-23 — Copy-to-clipboard on every result Added a small icon-only copy button ( ft.Icons.CONTENT_COPY , 16px icon in a 30x30 hit area) to all three result surfaces: the calculator display (top row of the display panel, left of the DEG/RAD toggle), the answer of each calculation history entry, and the unit conversion result field (as the TextField suffix ). Implementation: one shared ft.Clipboard() service created in main() , plus a copy_to_clipboard() helper and a make_copy_button(get_value) factory in src/main.py . The button reads its value at click time through a getter instead of baking the string into the control, so it cannot copy a stale value. Chosen over the ft.CopyToClipboard client action for that reason; the tradeoff is reliance on Clipboard.set() , which is silent on iOS Safari web builds — irrelevant for this desktop app, but relevant if it is ever published to the web. Feedback: ft.SnackBar via page.show_dialog , e.g. "Copied 3.14159…", truncating values past 40 chars. Empty surfaces report "Nothing to copy yet" rather than writing an empty string. The display's copy button is disabled while an error message is showing. Not covered, by request: the expression half of each history entry still only inserts into the display. Service registration confirmed later (2026-10-23, chain work): ft.Clipboard self-registers through Service.__post_init__ into the page's internal registry, readable as page._services._services — note page.services is a different list, so probes must look at the internal registry. calculator_spec.md gained a "Copy to clipboard" section. 2026-10-23 — Documentation hub created Moved anycalc project documentation into Trilium under the AI note, per DOCUMENTATION_REMINDER.txt . calculator_spec.md remains in the repo as the feature spec; this note tree is the explanation/design layer, not a replacement. Recorded the verified state of the app: stack, file layout, main.py architecture, limits, named variables, drawer navigation. Open items pyproject.toml floats ( >=1.0.4 ): a fresh install — and the Linux bundle built today — resolve Flet 1.0.5 while .venv is on 1.0.4. Both verified working; pin with == in [project].dependencies if exact reproducibility matters more than getting patches. Audit calculator_spec.md against src/main.py line-by-line and reconcile any drift (spec features not implemented, or implemented features missing from the spec). README.md now carries setup / run / build commands (it used to be empty). Decide whether it should also link this note tree, and whether build/ (≈625 MB of generated Flutter/app output) should be ignored once the project becomes a git repo — there is no top-level .gitignore yet. All app logic sits in one ~1,700-line main.py ; splitting the expression engine, conversion engine, and UI into modules is worth considering before the app grows further. There is no test suite in the repo. The formula-flip property check and the app drive-through probes currently live in /tmp and are throwaway; promoting them to pytest (the drive-through needs a Flet session, the pure logic does not) would make the conversion engine safe to refactor. Importing src/main.py no longer launches the app — the module now ends in def run_app() behind an if __name__ == "__main__": guard, so the engines are importable; the dev extra in pyproject.toml already lists pytest. The = morph animation was verified only as control state (sizes, colours, offsets, opacity, timings), not visually — the lift distance ( PREVIEW_MORPH_LIFT ) and duration are the knobs to tune once it is watched in a running window. Drawer / dropdown / history ordering is never sorted — it is pure YAML file order (see the anycalc hub note's ordering table). Nothing decided yet about sorting alphabetically, adding an order: field, or making the unit dropdowns searchable. Trig in DEG mode is not exact ( sin(30) → 0.49999999999999994). Worth deciding whether the degree conversion should round cleanly, now that raw results are shown live. 2026-10-23 — Volume, liquid and weight conversion groups added (high accuracy). src/assets/conversions.yaml : new Volume unit group (39 units) + Volume Conversion (40 formulas), new Weight unit group (23 units) + Weight Conversion (22 formulas). No .py change needed — groups are data-driven; conversion_options is derived from the YAML, so the new entries land in the drawer's Conversion block in file order (positions 5-6) and the calculator DrawerItemIndex mapping is unaffected. Coverage: metric cubic/liquid/culinary, US customary liquid + dry, imperial liquid, cubic in/ft/yd/mi, acre-foot, petroleum barrel; metric/avoirdupois/troy/apothecaries' mass, stone, hundredweights, short & long tons, carat, quintal. Every factor is the legal definition kept exact (NIST SP 811 / 1959 yard-and-pound): in³ = 16.387064 cm³, US gal = 231 in³, US dry gal = 268.8025 in³, imp gal = 4.54609 L, lb = 0.45359237 kg, gr = 0.00006479891 kg, oz t = 480 gr. Long exact values are chained through integers because the engine parses literals via Decimal(str(float)) (15-digit cap); US tbsp/tsp got direct mL definitions so no route has to divide by 3 first. Verified: config loads, 1988 unit pairs all reachable, 672/672 + 247/247 terminating-decimal pairs reproduced bit-exactly, 41/41 published-value spot checks, app launches clean ( timeout 30 .venv/bin/flet run , no traceback; build/ is absent so the dev client is used). Docs: calculator_spec.md gained a "Volume and weight conversions" section (exactness rules), README.md gained a "Unit conversions" section. Probe scripts live in /tmp ( probe_volwt.py , probe_sweep.py , probe_exact.py ) — still candidates for promotion to pytest once the dev extra can be installed. 2026-10-24 — % on the regular pad, ± on both pads Requested: a % button on the regular calculator, and a ± button on both calculators ( ± confirmed as the right glyph — it is the standard sign-change key; iOS writes the same key as "+/-"). What the app does now Regular keypad: AC ⌫ ( ) ± % on the utility row, then the unchanged digit/operator rows. Putting the two new keys in the existing top row instead of adding a row keeps the pad exactly as tall as before, which matters because the pad already fills the window in scientific mode. Scientific keypad: no duplicate keys. The scientific block is now sin cos tan √ / log ln π e ^ / Set Variable, Insert Variable above the regular rows — ( , ) , % and ± come from the shared utility row, so nothing is printed twice and every key-<label> stays unique (previously ( and ) were duplicated in scientific mode). % inserts Python's modulo, the same as the scientific key always did: 9%2 → 1, 7%2.5 → 2. Decimal 's remainder truncates the quotient, so the result keeps the dividend's sign ( -7%2 → -1, 7%-2 → 1) rather than Python's floor remainder ( -7 % 2 == 1 ); 5%0 reports "Invalid result". Not percent-of ( x/100 ) — flagging that as the open product question. ± is new logic in toggle_sign() (module-level, so it is unit-testable without an app): it edits rather than appends. It flips the sign of the last number typed, or of the result right after = ; 5*3 → 5*-3 ; a second press removes the sign instead of stacking one ( 5--3 → 5-3 ); if the expression ends on an operator the sign goes at the end for the number about to be typed ( 5- → 5-- , so typing 3 gives 5 − (−3)); a numberless expression is untouched. Pressing ± never leaves result mode, so -5 straight after = is still a result. Keypad key handling: ± is handled before the "any other key starts a new entry" block in press() , and the ⌫ / AC /error paths are unchanged. Docs: calculator_spec.md gained a "Calculator keypad" section (keys per pad, one-key-once rule, no height growth, % semantics incl. the dividend sign, all ± rules) plus a Testing bullet about the expression-engine file; README.md lists the new test file. No data/YAML changes. 2026-10-24 — % on the Regular Calculator is now a desk-calculator percent key; Length factors made exact Requested: the regular calculator's % should behave like the percent key on a physical desk calculator (the earlier entry above flagged "percent-of vs modulo" as the open product question — this settles it), and the Length group's rounded conversion factors should be replaced by their exact legal anchors. Decision: % means two different things, one per pad. The Regular Calculator gets desk-calculator percent; the Scientific Calculator keeps the modulo operator, because there % is used as a programming operator and percent would be useless. What the app does now (Regular pad) 50% → 0.5; 200+10% → 220 and 200-10% → 180 (the share of the number on its left); 200*10% → 20 and 200/10% → 2000 (plain fraction); chaining re-applies the rule to the running total, so 200+10%+5% → 231. Pressing % with nothing in front of it does nothing, and a lone % shows an error instead of a traceback. Implementation: a postfix % is not Python syntax, so apply_percent_operators() rewrites it into a marker call before parsing — 200+10% becomes 200+_percent(10) — walking back over the digits, or over a parenthesised call such as sqrt(4)% . evaluate() divides a bare marker call by 100, and percent_share() turns + _percent(n) / - _percent(n) into that share of the already-evaluated left operand. Only the regular pad is rewritten ( calculate() applies it when scientific is False), so the scientific pad's modulo is untouched. ± had to learn the same distinction, otherwise it would treat the regular pad's % as an unfinished operator: toggle_sign() takes a percent_is_modulo flag, so 200+10% negates its last number while 9% on the scientific pad is mid-entry and gets the sign at the end. Unparsable input now reports ERROR_INVALID_EXPRESSION ("Invalid expression") instead of the bare "Error". Unit conversion data ( **src/assets/conversions.yaml** , Length group) Rounded literals replaced by the legal anchors: inch → millimetre is x * 25.4 (was meter → inch = x * 39.37007874 ), mile → metre is x * 1609.344 (was x / 1.150779448 for mile → nautical mile), nautical_mile → metre is x * 1852 , light_year → metre is the exact integer x * 9460730472580800 , AU stays 149597870.7 km. So inch → millimetre is now exactly 25.4 instead of 25.4000000001…, and nautical mile → metre exactly 1852 instead of 1851.9999994…. Integer literals are exact however long, because the engine parses an int constant through Decimal(str(int)) ; only decimal literals are capped at the 15 significant digits that survive float parsing. That is why the light-year is written as a 16-digit integer and the parsec keeps 13 digits ( x / 3.2615637771674 ). The parsec is the one Length hop that cannot be exact at all: it is 648000/π astronomical units, hence not a rational number. It is excluded from the exactness sweep by name, with the reason in the YAML comment and in the test. Tests tests/test_calculator_engine.py : 56 → 96 tests, % split into a percent block (regular) and a modulo block (scientific), plus direct coverage of apply_percent_operators and is_percent_call . tests/test_conversion_engine.py : 75 → 82 tests; LENGTH_DRIFT and its xfail(strict=True) marker deleted, exactness sweep extended over the whole Length group (parsec excepted). tests/test_app.py : 6 → 7 UI tests; the keypad test asserts 200+10% previews 220 on the regular pad and the scientific assertions keep 9%2 at 1 . Verified: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -k engine → 178 passed in ~3 s. Docs: calculator_spec.md — the Length "known deviation" paragraph is replaced by the exact-anchor rule plus the parsec exception, the "Calculator keypad" section splits % per pad and extends the ± mid-entry rule, and the Testing section records the removed marker. README.md — exact anchors + parsec caveat, -k engine now selects both engine files, percent/modulo described in the test bullet. Trilium: the "Testing — pytest + flet test suite" note is rewritten to match; this entry is appended here because the note editor only offers whole-note rewrite or append for rich-text notes (the newest-at-top convention is broken by this placement, not by the content). Correction to the entry above (checked against the code after writing it): a lone % does not report an error. apply_percent_operators drops a % that has no operand in front of it, calculate() then sees an empty program and returns 0 , so the display simply stays at zero. The "Invalid expression" error is what a % typed straight after another operator produces once = is pressed ( 5+% → rewritten to 5+ → syntax error). 2026-10-24 — single-file app split into 11 modules; src re-registered inside packaged builds The split (spec §"Source layout", done for real this time) src/main.py was 1607 lines holding everything; it is now 52 lines (entry only: main(page) , run_app() , the __main__ guard). New modules, matching the module names the spec already listed: config.py (constants + Decimal precision + CONVERSION_CONFIG_PATH ), calculate.py (expression engine, 426 lines), conversions.py (conversion config + route finding, 350), ui.py ( CalculatorApp state/display/preview/mode wiring, 668), keypad.py (both pads' rows + make_key ), conversion_view.py ( ConversionView ), history_view.py , variable_dialogs.py , clipboard.py ( ClipboardService ), styles.py , __init__.py . Dependency direction is one-way: engines import only config ; ui imports engines + views + keypad/clipboard/dialogs; views and dialogs receive what they need (page, controls, callbacks, or the app object) instead of reaching into an app closure. No engine imports Flet, so tests/test_calculator_engine.py / test_conversion_engine.py still run under plain pytest . Code was moved verbatim (only indentation and the closure-variable → self. translation), so behaviour could not drift: flet test → 185 passed (7 test_app.py + 178 engine tests), and the test files needed no changes at all — their from src.conversions import … imports were already correct from the previous phase. Packaging gotcha found on the way (this is the part worth remembering) flet test / flet build copy the app folder itself ( [tool.flet.app] path = "src" ) flat into build/flet/tests/app/ and put that folder , not the project root, on sys.path ( _prepare_temp_dir , _copy_project_files_into / _copy_python_app_files_into in flet_cli/commands/build_base.py , plus _build_pth() ). So in a built app the modules are top-level ( main , ui , styles , …) and from src.ui import CalculatorApp fails: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'src.ui' raised from __main__ (it also silently degrades python -m src.main — run that from src/ and you get a second, duplicate copy of every module, because sys.path[0] becomes src/ ). Fix lives only in src/main.py , before every other import: _ensure_src_package() registers src in sys.modules as a package whose __path__ is the folder holding the entry module. One set of absolute src. imports then works both when the tree is imported as src.* from the workspace root and when the flattened artifact runs as __main__ . Nothing else in the codebase knows how the app was packaged. Verified three ways: host import ( python -c "import src.main" ), a flattened-directory simulation of the bundle ( cd into it, python main.py , assert src.__path__ points at the bundle and that the sibling assets/conversions.yaml still resolves), and flet test (which builds first) → all green. src/assets/conversions.yaml keeps resolving because config.py builds the path from Path(__file__) , and the copy step keeps assets/ next to the modules. Docs: calculator_spec.md §"Packaging & entry point" gained the import-root rule and the "registration lives in the entry module only" rule. Disk: 225 GB free → ~221 GB; AVD data in ~/.android/avd/anycalc.avd . 2026-10-26 — "Emulator is not responding" was the host, not the app The Android emulator window repeatedly triggered an "is not responding" dialog while AnythingCalculator itself ran perfectly (verified: 21 scripted taps all landed, display showed 444444444444444444444 , screenshot had no dialog). The dialog is not Android's and not the emulator's. The string "not responding" appears nowhere in the emulator binaries except an unrelated Qt WebEngine library, and the guest reported 0 ANR in entries even under a 50-tap burst, never lost mCurrentFocus . It is the GNOME Shell X11 liveness watchdog: org.gnome.mutter check-alive-timeout , default 5000 ms . The emulator's Qt window is an X11 client under XWayland, so any stall over 5 s gets the window declared dead. What caused the stalls. Host saturation: clamscan was pinned at 99 % of a core, VS Code's renderer spiked to 100 %, 4 vCPU guest on a 4-core host, and ~6 GB swapped with heavy I/O. The emulator also runs niced at +5 while gnome-shell runs at −5 , so under contention the emulator is the first thing starved (negative nice is denied to this user, so it cannot be counteracted from the shell). KVM was never the problem. My "0 kvm threads" reading was a bad grep . Proof of hardware acceleration: the process fds /dev/kvm , kvm-vm and kvm-vcpu:0/1/2 , and its log line CPU Acceleration status: KVM (version 12) is installed and usable plus QEMU's -enable-kvm -smp cores=4 -m 4096 . Changes made: AVD hw.cpu.ncore 4 → 3 (leave a core for the host), hw.ramSize 4096 → 3072 MB, emulator launched without -verbose (that flag logged a DEBUG line per rendered frame: 1131 debug lines vs 8 warnings), and check-alive-timeout 5000 → 20000 ms so brief host stalls stop being reported. The RAM/core change invalidates the default_boot snapshot, so the next boot is cold (31 s). Measured afterwards on a quiet host: 50 taps at 45 ms round-trip, 0 ANRs, boot 31 s (vs 40 s with the scan running), emulator log 11 KB instead of 139 KB. The emulator's own exit path is a stall too: it saved the default_boot snapshot in 3902 ms on quit, which alone nearly trips a 5 s watchdog. Mechanism confirmed, not guessed - the frozen thing is the event loop , not the pixels. The check is EWMH _NET_WM_PING : gsettings describe org.gnome.mutter check-alive-timeout reads "Number of milliseconds a client has to respond to a ping request in order to not be detected as frozen"; libmutter-18.so.0 carries the _NET_WM_PING / WM_PROTOCOLS / check-alive-timeout strings; the XWayland root window on :0 advertises _NET_WM_PING in _NET_SUPPORTED ; and each of the emulator's own top-level windows ( 0x3000007 device screen "Android Emulator - anycalc:5554", 0x300001a "Extended Controls", 0x300000a toolbar) lists _NET_WM_PING in its WM_PROTOCOLS . So the compositor pings the window and waits for the Qt event loop to echo it back - rendering is a separate thread and keeps running, which is exactly why the screen looked perfect, taps still round-tripped in 45 ms and the guest logged 0 ANRs while a dialog was up. The emulator process owns four pingable top-level windows, so the dialog may have been about the toolbar or Extended Controls window rather than the device screen. -no-window ("disable graphical window display") removes the X11 client entirely - the only setting under which the desktop can never complain; screenshots still work via adb exec-out screencap -p . 2026-10-26 — keypad keys got a Material ink ripple (press feedback was missing) Symptom: tapping a calculator key changed only the display; the key tile itself showed nothing. Next to the header's hamburger/history buttons — which are real IconButton s and ripple — the pad looked dead. Cause, not a regression: make_key() in src/keypad.py returns a bare ft.Container(on_click=...) . A Flet Container has no press feedback unless ink=True , which wraps it in Material + InkWell . git log -p over keypad.py shows ink was never set, so this was missing from the start rather than broken by a later change. Fix: src/keypad.py — ink=True , ink_color=KEY_INK on the key Container , plus a docstring paragraph explaining that a bare Container tap target needs ink explicitly. src/styles.py — KEY_INK = "#40FFFFFF" . Why that colour: Flutter 3.44's dark theme hardcodes the default splash to #40CCCCCC (25% grey) — it is not derived from colorScheme.primary , so the theme alone cannot make the ripple visible here. #40FFFFFF keeps the same 25% alpha but uses neutral white, which stays visible on the accent blue = ( #4F7DFF ) and the maroon AC ( #7B3340 ) as well as on the dark keys. Verification: flet test -k engine → 178 passed (the suite never covered press feedback, and still cannot — it asserts texts/keys, not rendering). The visual proof came from the Android emulator route: holding a touch with adb shell input motionevent DOWN , capturing with adb exec-out screencap -p , then motionevent UP , which caught the white ripple mid-spread across 8 , 9 and = while the press still committed. Spec: the keypad section of calculator_spec.md now states the requirement — every key acknowledges a press visually through the ripple, on the key itself, not only in the display that changes. Commit: a2c7729 Add Material ink ripple feedback to keypad keys (the testing-path docs are the separate d72443e ). 2026-10-31 — pi page: a bar weighted by work, a progress card on a clock, and a paged digits dialog Symptoms reported: "the progress bar isnt moving", then "the progress only updates when a button is pressed — make it update every 0.5s automatically", and "what is going on with these scrollboxes in the view digits". The bar, cause 1 — it was weighted by terms. fraction divided terms done by terms total, so it stood near two thirds through the whole tail (the products that combine the terms, the last square root, the division) and then snapped to 100 %: it looked finished, or stuck, long before the run was. It now divides measured work ( work_done / work_total ) — the binary split knows what it costs before the first term ( pi.run_weight ), so a run has an honest percentage from the start. The bar, cause 2 — its track was the card's own colour. bgcolor=CARD_BACKGROUND made the unfilled part invisible, so a filling bar read as a growing blob. Now bgcolor=PANEL_BACKGROUND , bar_height=10 — exactly what the spec already demanded. The bar, cause 3 — nothing was pushing it on the clock. The worker's report callback was the only painter, and one huge multiplication produces no report at all, so the card sat still for precisely the longest stretch of a run. Now: start_run schedules _paint_loop with page.run_task — the page's own event loop, not a second page.run_thread . run_thread queues on an executor shared with every other handler in the app, so a painter can sit waiting for a worker slot; a painter that never got one is a bar that seems to move only when something else repaints the page. self._paint_task keeps the reference, because an unreferenced task can be collected mid-run. The half second is anchored to a schedule ( loop.time() + PROGRESS_PAINT_SECONDS each pass) rather than a chain of time.sleep s: a loop sharing the interpreter with a computation over huge integers wakes late by tens of milliseconds at a time, and chained sleeps add that lateness up until the card drifts to a paint every two thirds of a second. The rate cap lives inside _paint_progress , not in either caller, so the clock and the engine's checkpoints spend one shared budget of two frames a second. The worker still paints with each report — a checkpoint is often the only progress that can be shown while the interpreter is busy with one multiplication — but a million reports cannot become a million page updates. _last_paint is reset in __init__ and start_run (a stale stamp from a previous run would otherwise swallow the first frames of the next), and _card_final stands the painter down the moment a run ends, so a late tick can never write a mid-run number over what a finished or cancelled run reports. The clock survives a frame that fails to reach the client : the tick is wrapped, the task keeps asking on schedule and the status line says progress display failed: … . An unwrapped await -task dies on one exception and says nothing — which is precisely the reported symptom, a bar that only moves when a button handler happens to repaint the page. The digits view, cause — the list grew under the reader's fingers. The dialog used one endless list extended on every scroll event ( _fill_more_on_scroll , a batch at a time). A scrollbar can only be honest about a length that does not move: that list kept re-measuring a distance that changed mid-drag, so the thumb resized while it was being dragged, the end kept running away from it, and the thumb ended up a meaningless sliver. There is no scroll handler left: the dialog holds one page of DIALOG_PAGE_DECIMALS = 10_000 decimals, which is replaced rather than appended when the reader turns a page, with First / Previous / Next / Last buttons (disabled when there is nowhere to go), a footline saying where they are ("decimals 10 001 to 20 000 of 60 000 — page 2 of 6"), a page turn that returns the scroll to the top of the new page, and DIALOG_SCROLLBAR_GUTTER = 14 so the thumb no longer draws on top of the digits it is about. A hundred million decimals are still never on screen at once. Measured in the running app, with nothing pressed (a temporary probe driving the real AnycalcApp , screenshots through page.take_screenshot() ): * 20 000 000 digits: the card read 4.7 % → 8.6 % → 13.1 % → 19.4 % → 24.2 % → 30.5 % → 38.7 % → 43.9 % at 2 s intervals, and every screenshot differed from the one before it (33–114 changed sample pixels across the frame). * Counting repaints directly: 60 repaints in 46.7 s on that run, ~2 a second between samples; a 1 000 000-digit run took 4 repaints in 1.9 s = 2.16 a second , i.e. the full rate the cap allows. * Cadence, measured as the gap between repaints on a 20 000 000-digit run (43 repaints, nothing pressed): 0.502, 0.500, 0.508, 0.542, 0.503, 0.507, 0.509 … — the card moves on the half second. The exceptions are the ones physics allows: 0.92 s, 1.22 s and, inside the final square root and division, up to 4.5 s, because a single C-level multiplication of numbers that size holds the interpreter and no Python code at all can run in between. Screenshots at 4 s, 8 s, 12 s, 16 s and 20 s of that run (25.4 % with 652 284 / 1 410 275 terms and "about 24 s left", then 100 % and "took 34 s") differ from each other in every byte. Tests ( tests/test_pi_view.py , 59 pass): the painter is a task and not a thread; a run's card paints about twice a second with no report and no press; a tick and a report never cost two frames in one half second; a thousand reports cost at most two frames; a finished run keeps its own words against a late tick; plus the paging rules (page math, replaced-not-appended lines, both ends unreachable by pressing, short last page never padded, one-page numbers have nowhere to turn). test_a_thousand_reports_cost_at_most_two_frames and the tick/report test are new for this change. 2026-10-31 — docs migrated into docs/ (MkDocs); the first commit of them un-pushed for PII What happened: the project notes were migrated out of Trilium notes into docs/ with a mkdocs.yml at the root. The whole set — plus the generated site/ output — was committed and pushed before being scrubbed . What it exposed: the Linux account name, carried in a Flet app id ( com.<personal>.anycalc and its .desktop file id), in an absolute home path ( /home/<user>/Android/Sdk ), in /dev/kvm ACL output, and in /tmp paths derived from the account name ( hsperfdata_<user> , <user>-code-zsh , android-<user> ). The same text existed twice : once in docs/ , again in the committed site/ HTML and in site/search/search_index.json , which flattens every page into one searchable blob. The undo: the leak was the tip commit, so git push --force-with-lease=main:<leaked SHA> took it off origin/main in one step. Verified afterwards: no forks, no PRs, no Pages site, no branch protection — and every blob of every commit reachable from the restored tip matches none of the PII patterns, so the published chain is clean. GitHub may keep serving the unreachable commit by SHA until it garbage-collects; that is the one part outside our control. The SHA is deliberately not quoted here. Scrub rule applied to the docs: current-state pages carry the real handle-based id ( com.github.greentruck50.anycalc ); change-log entries that describe the old id keep it neutral ( com.<personal> , <org>.anycalc.desktop , $HOME -relative paths, <user> placeholders) — substituting the new value into a historical sentence would make the sentence false. site/ is build output, not source: the staged copy is deleted and regenerated with .venv/bin/mkdocs build (mkdocs 1.6.1). Never hand-edit it, and treat it as a publishing surface — it mirrors every word of docs/ , so it carries the identical PII exposure. Spec: the pi section of calculator_spec.md now requires the half-second repaint on the page's own event loop, the schedule rather than chained sleeps, the one shared two-frames-a-second budget across clock and checkpoints, and the card belonging to the outcome once a run ends; and for the digits dialog it forbids growing the list while it is scrolled and requires the page buttons, the footline and the scrollbar gutter.

docs.text: Was flet>=1.0.4 + PyYAML>=6.0.3 ; now flet[cli,desktop]>=1.0.4 + PyYAML>=6.0.3 , each with a comment saying what it is for. Reason: in Flet 1.x the desktop runtime is an extra , not a dependency. Plain flet pulls only httpx , msgpack , oauthlib , repath ; ft.run() then calls ensure_flet_desktop_package_installed() ( flet/app.py:305 → flet/utils/pip.py:88 ), which pip-installs flet-desktop behind your back on first launch. Declaring the extra keeps a fresh install deterministic and offline-safe, and Flet pins its extras to its own exact version, so the bracket group can never drift from the SDK. [cli] is included because the app is launched with flet run . [web] is deliberately not included (it would drag in fastapi / uvicorn / websockets for a target this desktop app does not ship). [test] (pytest, pytest-asyncio, numpy, pillow, scikit-image) is dev tooling and stays out. Audited every import in src/ (re-checked during the pyproject migration): everything else is stdlib ( ast , asyncio , math , operator , collections , dataclasses , decimal , pathlib , typing ), so nothing was missing besides the Flet extras. Transitive deps are left to pip. Verified from scratch: a clean venv built only from requirements.txt resolved flet 1.0.5 + flet-cli / flet-desktop / flet-platform-assets 1.0.5 + PyYAML 6.0.3 , pip check clean, and the full headless UI probe passed in that venv — so the app is good on 1.0.5 too, not just the 1.0.4 in .venv .

docs.text: Unit conversions no longer have a "Convert" button. run_conversion() is wired to the value field's on_change and to both unit dropdowns' on_select , so the result and the chain of operations refresh the moment the value or a unit changes. A small hint line ("Converts as you type or change units" with a swap icon) took the button's place. Typing noise is silent: an empty value or something that is not a number yet ( - , 3. , abc ) clears the result and the chain without setting a field error; only genuine failures such as having no valid route still surface as result_field.error . The old "Enter a value to convert" error, the "Select both a source and target unit" check and clear_conversion_output() were removed. Both calculators now show a live answer: a small grey ( #9CA3AF , 15 px) number under the expression box that re-evaluates the expression on every change. preview_answer() returns "" for an empty expression, one that cannot be evaluated yet (half-typed), one that is already a single number, or an error message — refresh_preview() hides the slot in those cases. Hooked into every path that can change the expression or what it means: update_display() (keypad, history insert, variable insert), handle_display_change() (typing), toggle_angle() (DEG/RAD), assign_variable() (a new variable value), and set_mode() , which resets the slot. Pressing = does not make that number vanish. promote_preview() grows it to the display size (34), turns it white, slides it up PREVIEW_MORPH_LIFT = 34 px and fades it out over PREVIEW_MORPH_MS = 260 ms using Flet implicit animations ( animate_size / animate_offset / animate_opacity with ft.AnimationStyle(duration=…, curve=ft.AnimationCurve.EASE_OUT_CUBIC) ). The display already holds the answer during the morph, so the two converge instead of anything disappearing. Morph cleanup: page.run_task(finish_preview_morph, token) resets the slot after the animation; the token makes a stale timer a no-op, and the preview_morphing flag keeps refresh_preview() from fighting an animation in flight. All tunables are module constants at the top of main.py . The display panel grew 140 → 168 px for the preview line; asyncio was added to the imports (stdlib, so no dependency change). Verified with a headless Flet drive-through ( /tmp/live_probe.py ): no Convert button in the tree; typing 2500 cm → km gives 0.025 with a 2-hop chain; "-" and "abc" clear silently with no errors; changing From to metre re-converts 5 → 0.005 without touching the value; the same-unit zero-step card still appears. Calculator: preview shows 4 for "2+2" and 25 for "2+23"; after = the display reads 25 while the preview is at 34 px / white / opacity 0 / offset −34 and still visible; ~0.5 s later the slot is hidden again at 15 px, offset 0, opacity 1. Reason (user request): the cards were busy — the formula was always visible even when it was not wanted, and announcing "applied backwards" is redundant once the formula itself is presented in the direction it was used. Implementation: _flip_conversion_formula() builds the reversed formula as an AST and unparses it, mirroring the algebra of _invert_conversion_formula() (+ ↔ −, × ↔ ÷). Dividing by a fraction is rewritten as multiplying by its reciprocal, so (x * 9/5) + 32 flips to (x - 32) * 5 / 9 and (x - 32) * 5/9 flips to x * 9 / 5 + 32 . ConversionStep gained applied_formula (the configured text is still kept in formula ); describe_conversion_step() was deleted. Verified two ways: a property check over all 76 MD formulas in conversions.yaml (every flip round-trips numerically through the app's own evaluator and agrees with the numeric solver), and a headless Flet session driving the real UI — formulas hidden until clicked, one button per hop, reveal/hide toggle, flipped formula on a reversed hop, a mixed 3-hop chain (Rankine → Kelvin), zero-step chain with no buttons, chain cleared on unit change, error path intact. docs.text: Requested: a % button on the regular calculator, and a ± button on both calculators ( ± confirmed as the right glyph — it is the standard sign-change key; iOS writes the same key as "+/-"). What the app does now Regular keypad: AC ⌫ ( ) ± % on the utility row, then the unchanged digit/operator rows. Putting the two new keys in the existing top row instead of adding a row keeps the pad exactly as tall as before, which matters because the pad already fills the window in scientific mode. Scientific keypad: no duplicate keys. The scientific block is now sin cos tan √ / log ln π e ^ / Set Variable, Insert Variable above the regular rows — ( , ) , % and ± come from the shared utility row, so nothing is printed twice and every key-<label> stays unique (previously ( and ) were duplicated in scientific mode). % inserts Python's modulo, the same as the scientific key always did: 9%2 → 1, 7%2.5 → 2. Decimal 's remainder truncates the quotient, so the result keeps the dividend's sign ( -7%2 → -1, 7%-2 → 1) rather than Python's floor remainder ( -7 % 2 == 1 ); 5%0 reports "Invalid result". Not percent-of ( x/100 ) — flagging that as the open product question. ± is new logic in toggle_sign() (module-level, so it is unit-testable without an app): it edits rather than appends. It flips the sign of the last number typed, or of the result right after = ; 5*3 → 5*-3 ; a second press removes the sign instead of stacking one ( 5--3 → 5-3 ); if the expression ends on an operator the sign goes at the end for the number about to be typed ( 5- → 5-- , so typing 3 gives 5 − (−3)); a numberless expression is untouched. Pressing ± never leaves result mode, so -5 straight after = is still a result. Keypad key handling: ± is handled before the "any other key starts a new entry" block in press() , and the ⌫ / AC /error paths are unchanged. Docs: calculator_spec.md gained a "Calculator keypad" section (keys per pad, one-key-once rule, no height growth, % semantics incl. the dividend sign, all ± rules) plus a Testing bullet about the expression-engine file; README.md lists the new test file. docs.text: Requested: the regular calculator's % should behave like the percent key on a physical desk calculator (the earlier entry above flagged "percent-of vs modulo" as the open product question — this settles it), and the Length group's rounded conversion factors should be replaced by their exact legal anchors. Decision: % means two different things, one per pad. The Regular Calculator gets desk-calculator percent; the Scientific Calculator keeps the modulo operator, because there % is used as a programming operator and percent would be useless. What the app does now (Regular pad) 50% → 0.5; 200+10% → 220 and 200-10% → 180 (the share of the number on its left); 200*10% → 20 and 200/10% → 2000 (plain fraction); chaining re-applies the rule to the running total, so 200+10%+5% → 231. Pressing % with nothing in front of it does nothing, and a lone % shows an error instead of a traceback. Implementation: a postfix % is not Python syntax, so apply_percent_operators() rewrites it into a marker call before parsing — 200+10% becomes 200+_percent(10) — walking back over the digits, or over a parenthesised call such as sqrt(4)% . evaluate() divides a bare marker call by 100, and percent_share() turns + _percent(n) / - _percent(n) into that share of the already-evaluated left operand. Only the regular pad is rewritten ( calculate() applies it when scientific is False), so the scientific pad's modulo is untouched. ± had to learn the same distinction, otherwise it would treat the regular pad's % as an unfinished operator: toggle_sign() takes a percent_is_modulo flag, so 200+10% negates its last number while 9% on the scientific pad is mid-entry and gets the sign at the end. Unparsable input now reports ERROR_INVALID_EXPRESSION ("Invalid expression") instead of the bare "Error". Unit conversion data ( **src/assets/conversions.yaml** , Length group) Rounded literals replaced by the legal anchors: inch → millimetre is x * 25.4 (was meter → inch = x * 39.37007874 ), mile → metre is x * 1609.344 (was x / 1.150779448 for mile → nautical mile), nautical_mile → metre is x * 1852 , light_year → metre is the exact integer x * 9460730472580800 , AU stays 149597870.7 km. So inch → millimetre is now exactly 25.4 instead of 25.4000000001…, and nautical mile → metre exactly 1852 instead of 1851.9999994…. Integer literals are exact however long, because the engine parses an int constant through Decimal(str(int)) ; only decimal literals are capped at the 15 significant digits that survive float parsing. That is why the light-year is written as a 16-digit integer and the parsec keeps 13 digits ( x / 3.2615637771674 ). The parsec is the one Length hop that cannot be exact at all: it is 648000/π astronomical units, hence not a rational number. It is excluded from the exactness sweep by name, with the reason in the YAML comment and in the test. Tests tests/test_calculator_engine.py : 56 → 96 tests, % split into a percent block (regular) and a modulo block (scientific), plus direct coverage of apply_percent_operators and is_percent_call . tests/test_conversion_engine.py : 75 → 82 tests; LENGTH_DRIFT and its xfail(strict=True) marker deleted, exactness sweep extended over the whole Length group (parsec excepted). tests/test_app.py : 6 → 7 UI tests; the keypad test asserts 200+10% previews 220 on the regular pad and the scientific assertions keep 9%2 at 1 . Verified: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -k engine → 178 passed in ~3 s. Docs: calculator_spec.md — the Length "known deviation" paragraph is replaced by the exact-anchor rule plus the parsec exception, the "Calculator keypad" section splits % per pad and extends the ± mid-entry rule, and the Testing section records the removed marker. README.md — exact anchors + parsec caveat, -k engine now selects both engine files, percent/modulo described in the test bullet. Trilium: the "Testing — pytest + flet test suite" note is rewritten to match; this entry is appended here because the note editor only offers whole-note rewrite or append for rich-text notes (the newest-at-top convention is broken by this placement, not by the content). Correction to the entry above (checked against the code after writing it): a lone % does not report an error. apply_percent_operators drops a % that has no operand in front of it, calculate() then sees an empty program and returns 0 , so the display simply stays at zero. The "Invalid expression" error is what a % typed straight after another operator produces once = is pressed ( 5+% → rewritten to 5+ → syntax error).

docs.text: The split (spec §"Source layout", done for real this time) src/main.py was 1607 lines holding everything; it is now 52 lines (entry only: main(page) , run_app() , the __main__ guard). New modules, matching the module names the spec already listed: config.py (constants + Decimal precision + CONVERSION_CONFIG_PATH ), calculate.py (expression engine, 426 lines), conversions.py (conversion config + route finding, 350), ui.py ( CalculatorApp state/display/preview/mode wiring, 668), keypad.py (both pads' rows + make_key ), conversion_view.py ( ConversionView ), history_view.py , variable_dialogs.py , clipboard.py ( ClipboardService ), styles.py , __init__.py . Dependency direction is one-way: engines import only config ; ui imports engines + views + keypad/clipboard/dialogs; views and dialogs receive what they need (page, controls, callbacks, or the app object) instead of reaching into an app closure. No engine imports Flet, so tests/test_calculator_engine.py / test_conversion_engine.py still run under plain pytest . Code was moved verbatim (only indentation and the closure-variable → self. translation), so behaviour could not drift: flet test → 185 passed (7 test_app.py + 178 engine tests), and the test files needed no changes at all — their from src.conversions import … imports were already correct from the previous phase. Packaging gotcha found on the way (this is the part worth remembering) flet test / flet build copy the app folder itself ( [tool.flet.app] path = "src" ) flat into build/flet/tests/app/ and put that folder , not the project root, on sys.path ( _prepare_temp_dir , _copy_project_files_into / _copy_python_app_files_into in flet_cli/commands/build_base.py , plus _build_pth() ). So in a built app the modules are top-level ( main , ui , styles , …) and from src.ui import CalculatorApp fails: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'src.ui' raised from __main__ (it also silently degrades python -m src.main — run that from src/ and you get a second, duplicate copy of every module, because sys.path[0] becomes src/ ). Fix lives only in src/main.py , before every other import: _ensure_src_package() registers src in sys.modules as a package whose __path__ is the folder holding the entry module. One set of absolute src. imports then works both when the tree is imported as src.* from the workspace root and when the flattened artifact runs as __main__ . Nothing else in the codebase knows how the app was packaged. Verified three ways: host import ( python -c "import src.main" ), a flattened-directory simulation of the bundle ( cd into it, python main.py , assert src.__path__ points at the bundle and that the sibling assets/conversions.yaml still resolves), and flet test (which builds first) → all green. src/assets/conversions.yaml keeps resolving because config.py builds the path from Path(__file__) , and the copy step keeps assets/ next to the modules. Docs: calculator_spec.md §"Packaging & entry point" gained the import-root rule and the "registration lives in the entry module only" rule. New subnote "Source layout — modules and the Flet import root" under the project note documents the module map and the gotcha. README.md already described the multi-module structure, so it needed no change (the code had drifted from it, not the other way round). Correction to the entry above (line counts re-checked with wc -l after writing it): src/main.py is 70 lines (not 52), ui.py 714 , calculate.py 389 , conversions.py 341 , config.py 107, conversion_view.py 268, variable_dialogs.py 206, history_view.py 104, keypad.py 90, clipboard.py 69, styles.py 23, __init__.py 6 — 12 modules, 2387 lines in src/ . The split also left the app's test totals confirmed at 185 passed under flet test and 178 passed for -k engine under plain pytest . One more clarification on the entry above: what "no test changes" means is that the tests were touched only for import paths , exactly as the spec's acceptance criterion allows. tests/test_calculator_engine.py imports src.calculate + src.config , tests/test_conversion_engine.py imports src.conversions , tests/test_app.py imports src.conversions — none of their assertions, fixtures or key selectors changed. That is the evidence the behaviour is unchanged: 7 UI tests + 178 engine tests green, both in the packaged app ( flet test ) and on the host ( pytest -k engine ). Corrections to the packaging notes above (re-checked against the installed flet-cli 1.0.5 source, 2026-10-24) The CLI internals named above — _prepare_temp_dir , _copy_project_files_into , _copy_python_app_files_into , _build_pth — do not exist in flet-cli 1.0.5. Those names were wrong. The real chain is: package_python_app() ( flet_cli/commands/build_base.py:2514 ) shells out to dart run serious_python:main package <Flet app dir> (args built ~2536-2543); the result is staged to **build/python-app/** , whose existence is verified at build_base.py:2843 , and that path is handed to the runner via the SERIOUS_PYTHON_APP env var ( build_base.py:2629 , :2999 ). The copying itself happens in the Dart-side serious_python tool, which is not installed in .venv . Direct evidence for the flattening, no inference needed — build/python-app/ on disk right now holds, all at one level: main.pyc, calculate.pyc, keypad.pyc, conversions.pyc, styles.pyc, ui.pyc, config.pyc, conversion_view.pyc, clipboard.pyc, variable_dialogs.pyc, history_view.pyc, __init__.pyc plus assets/conversions.yaml . __init__.pyc is present only because src/__init__.py exists, and it is what lets the entry module register src as a package rooted at that directory. Also stale: there is no **build/linux/** in the workspace any more , and today build/ is flutter 9.2 GB , site-packages 50 MB, python-app 188 KB, .hash , .python-version . The "132 MB artifact / 439 MB flutter" figures belonged to that one earlier run. How anycalc compares with a stock Flet app (ran flet create /tmp/tpl_probe with this project's own flet-cli, 2026-10-24) Stock scaffold = pyproject.toml , README.md , .gitignore , src/main.py , src/assets/icon.png , tests/test_main.py . So anycalc's folder shape is exactly the stock shape : entry is src/main.py , assets/ lives inside src/ , tests/ is a sibling of src/ , and [tool.flet.app] path = "src" (the template omits module — it defaults to main , we write it explicitly). Stock src/main.py also ends in if __name__ == "__main__": ft.run(main) , the same guard shape we use via run_app() . Stock scaffold does not have src/__init__.py , [tool.setuptools] or [project.scripts] . Crucially its pytest config is asyncio_mode = "auto" , testpaths = ["tests"] , **pythonpath = ["src"]** — stock Flet treats src/ as a sys.path root, not a package . So a multi-file stock app would import siblings as top-level names ( from ui import CalculatorApp ), which needs no shim because the packaged app dir is the same flattened directory put on sys.path . anycalc deliberately went the other way: src is a real package, absolute src.* imports everywhere, plus the _ensure_src_package() shim in the entry module. That is what makes pip install -e . and [project.scripts] anycalc = "src.main:run_app" meaningful; the price is one shim function. (Honest caveat: [tool.setuptools] packages = ["src"] installs a top-level package literally named src into site-packages, which is its own smell — the fully conventional fix would be src/anycalc/ .) Minor stock-config diffs we could adopt: [dependency-groups] dev = ["flet-cli", "flet-desktop", "flet-web", "flet[test]"] (PEP 735) instead of [project.optional-dependencies].dev ; requires-python = ">=3.10" (ours >=3.11 ); desktop_flavor = "light" , company , copyright keys; and stock tests/test_main.py never imports the app at all — it drives it purely through the flet_app fixture with find_by_key / find_by_text , which is how our test_app.py works too except for its one from src.conversions import load_conversion_config .

docs.text: Chosen action: scrub the first-name-based id out of every commit, not just the tip. Safety first: git bundle create ~/anycalc-pre-pii-rewrite.bundle --all before rewriting — 63 KB, verified with git bundle verify , contains the complete pre-rewrite history, so this is fully reversible. Push used --force-with-lease=main:<old SHA> so it could not clobber an unexpected remote state. Old → new SHA mapping (every SHA cited in earlier entries of this log is now stale; use this table): de014a9 → af158c5 , 5ff43bf → 94fc0a9 , 2af8a88 → 36bfca6 , 46a226d → 639d943 , fd3f2bd → 9218c1c (new tip). The root commit's content was untouched by the scrub but its hash changed anyway because it is an ancestor of changed commits... actually note: GitHub's "Initial commit" is on a merged side branch, so only ancestors of changed trees re-hash — the mapping above is what came out. Verification: after dropping refs/original/* (filter-branch keeps backups there — this is what made a first git grep over git rev-list --all still report the old string), then git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now , no reachable object in the local repo matches the string and all five old SHAs error as "Not a valid object name". .git is 256 KB / 62.78 KiB pack. git diff <old tip> <new tip> = empty , i.e. the rewrite changed no file content at HEAD; pytest -k engine still 178 passed. Honest caveat — GitHub has not purged the orphans. All 5 pre-rewrite commits are still fetchable by SHA on github.com even though the branch no longer references them and forks = 0, pulls = 0 . GitHub garbage-collects unreachable objects on its own schedule; a force-push alone does not delete them. If the old value must be gone now , the options are contacting GitHub Support, or deleting and recreating the repo. Also note the anycalc Trilium notes themselves still quote the old id (only fixable by rewriting those 28 KB / 73 KB rich-text notes whole — edit_note_content refuses text notes). Correction on why the untouched "Initial commit" got a new SHA: not ancestry — a commit hashes only its own tree, parents, identities, message and signature. git cat-file commit on the old ( 5ff43bf , recovered by cloning the pre-rewrite bundle into /tmp/oldrepo ) versus new ( 94fc0a9 ) shows identical tree, author, committer ( GitHub <noreply@github.com> ) and message, but the old object carried a gpgsig header (GitHub signed it when it created the commit) and filter-branch drops that header when re-writing the object. docs.text: The Android emulator window repeatedly triggered an "is not responding" dialog while AnythingCalculator itself ran perfectly (verified: 21 scripted taps all landed, display showed 444444444444444444444 , screenshot had no dialog). The dialog is not Android's and not the emulator's. The string "not responding" appears nowhere in the emulator binaries except an unrelated Qt WebEngine library, and the guest reported 0 ANR in entries even under a 50-tap burst, never lost mCurrentFocus . It is the GNOME Shell X11 liveness watchdog: org.gnome.mutter check-alive-timeout , default 5000 ms . The emulator's Qt window is an X11 client under XWayland, so any stall over 5 s gets the window declared dead. What caused the stalls. Host saturation: clamscan was pinned at 99 % of a core, VS Code's renderer spiked to 100 %, 4 vCPU guest on a 4-core host, and ~6 GB swapped with heavy I/O. The emulator also runs niced at +5 while gnome-shell runs at −5 , so under contention the emulator is the first thing starved (negative nice is denied to this user, so it cannot be counteracted from the shell). KVM was never the problem. My "0 kvm threads" reading was a bad grep . Proof of hardware acceleration: the process fds /dev/kvm , kvm-vm and kvm-vcpu:0/1/2 , and its log line CPU Acceleration status: KVM (version 12) is installed and usable plus QEMU's -enable-kvm -smp cores=4 -m 4096 . Changes made: AVD hw.cpu.ncore 4 → 3 (leave a core for the host), hw.ramSize 4096 → 3072 MB, emulator launched without -verbose (that flag logged a DEBUG line per rendered frame: 1131 debug lines vs 8 warnings), and check-alive-timeout 5000 → 20000 ms so brief host stalls stop being reported. The RAM/core change invalidates the default_boot snapshot, so the next boot is cold (31 s). Measured afterwards on a quiet host: 50 taps at 45 ms round-trip, 0 ANRs, boot 31 s (vs 40 s with the scan running), emulator log 11 KB instead of 139 KB. The emulator's own exit path is a stall too: it saved the default_boot snapshot in 3902 ms on quit, which alone nearly trips a 5 s watchdog. Mechanism confirmed, not guessed - the frozen thing is the event loop , not the pixels. The check is EWMH _NET_WM_PING : gsettings describe org.gnome.mutter check-alive-timeout reads "Number of milliseconds a client has to respond to a ping request in order to not be detected as frozen"; libmutter-18.so.0 carries the _NET_WM_PING / WM_PROTOCOLS / check-alive-timeout strings; the XWayland root window on :0 advertises _NET_WM_PING in _NET_SUPPORTED ; and each of the emulator's own top-level windows ( 0x3000007 device screen "Android Emulator - anycalc:5554", 0x300001a "Extended Controls", 0x300000a toolbar) lists _NET_WM_PING in its WM_PROTOCOLS . So the compositor pings the window and waits for the Qt event loop to echo it back - rendering is a separate thread and keeps running, which is exactly why the screen looked perfect, taps still round-tripped in 45 ms and the guest logged 0 ANRs while a dialog was up. The emulator process owns four pingable top-level windows, so the dialog may have been about the toolbar or Extended Controls window rather than the device screen. -no-window ("disable graphical window display") removes the X11 client entirely - the only setting under which the desktop can never complain; screenshots still work via adb exec-out screencap -p .

Next to the header's hamburger/history buttons — which are real IconButton s and ripple — the pad looked dead. docs.text: Symptoms reported: "the progress bar isnt moving", then "the progress only updates when a button is pressed — make it update every 0.5s automatically", and "what is going on with these scrollboxes in the view digits". The bar, cause 1 — it was weighted by terms. fraction divided terms done by terms total, so it stood near two thirds through the whole tail (the products that combine the terms, the last square root, the division) and then snapped to 100 %: it looked finished, or stuck, long before the run was. It now divides measured work ( work_done / work_total ) — the binary split knows what it costs before the first term ( pi.run_weight ), so a run has an honest percentage from the start. The bar, cause 2 — its track was the card's own colour. bgcolor=CARD_BACKGROUND made the unfilled part invisible, so a filling bar read as a growing blob. Now bgcolor=PANEL_BACKGROUND , bar_height=10 — exactly what the spec already demanded. The bar, cause 3 — nothing was pushing it on the clock. The worker's report callback was the only painter, and one huge multiplication produces no report at all, so the card sat still for precisely the longest stretch of a run. Now: start_run schedules _paint_loop with page.run_task — the page's own event loop, not a second page.run_thread . run_thread queues on an executor shared with every other handler in the app, so a painter can sit waiting for a worker slot; a painter that never got one is a bar that seems to move only when something else repaints the page. self._paint_task keeps the reference, because an unreferenced task can be collected mid-run. The half second is anchored to a schedule ( loop.time() + PROGRESS_PAINT_SECONDS each pass) rather than a chain of time.sleep s: a loop sharing the interpreter with a computation over huge integers wakes late by tens of milliseconds at a time, and chained sleeps add that lateness up until the card drifts to a paint every two thirds of a second. The rate cap lives inside _paint_progress , not in either caller, so the clock and the engine's checkpoints spend one shared budget of two frames a second. The worker still paints with each report — a checkpoint is often the only progress that can be shown while the interpreter is busy with one multiplication — but a million reports cannot become a million page updates. _last_paint is reset in __init__ and start_run (a stale stamp from a previous run would otherwise swallow the first frames of the next), and _card_final stands the painter down the moment a run ends, so a late tick can never write a mid-run number over what a finished or cancelled run reports. The clock survives a frame that fails to reach the client : the tick is wrapped, the task keeps asking on schedule and the status line says progress display failed: … . An unwrapped await -task dies on one exception and says nothing — which is precisely the reported symptom, a bar that only moves when a button handler happens to repaint the page. The digits view, cause — the list grew under the reader's fingers. The dialog used one endless list extended on every scroll event ( _fill_more_on_scroll , a batch at a time). A scrollbar can only be honest about a length that does not move: that list kept re-measuring a distance that changed mid-drag, so the thumb resized while it was being dragged, the end kept running away from it, and the thumb ended up a meaningless sliver. There is no scroll handler left: the dialog holds one page of DIALOG_PAGE_DECIMALS = 10_000 decimals, which is replaced rather than appended when the reader turns a page, with First / Previous / Next / Last buttons (disabled when there is nowhere to go), a footline saying where they are ("decimals 10 001 to 20 000 of 60 000 — page 2 of 6"), a page turn that returns the scroll to the top of the new page, and DIALOG_SCROLLBAR_GUTTER = 14 so the thumb no longer draws on top of the digits it is about. A hundred million decimals are still never on screen at once. Measured in the running app, with nothing pressed (a temporary probe driving the real AnycalcApp , screenshots through page.take_screenshot() ): * 20 000 000 digits: the card read 4.7 % → 8.6 % → 13.1 % → 19.4 % → 24.2 % → 30.5 % → 38.7 % → 43.9 % at 2 s intervals, and every screenshot differed from the one before it (33–114 changed sample pixels across the frame). * Counting repaints directly: 60 repaints in 46.7 s on that run, ~2 a second between samples; a 1 000 000-digit run took 4 repaints in 1.9 s = 2.16 a second , i.e. the full rate the cap allows. * Cadence, measured as the gap between repaints on a 20 000 000-digit run (43 repaints, nothing pressed): 0.502, 0.500, 0.508, 0.542, 0.503, 0.507, 0.509 … — the card moves on the half second. The exceptions are the ones physics allows: 0.92 s, 1.22 s and, inside the final square root and division, up to 4.5 s, because a single C-level multiplication of numbers that size holds the interpreter and no Python code at all can run in between. Screenshots at 4 s, 8 s, 12 s, 16 s and 20 s of that run (25.4 % with 652 284 / 1 410 275 terms and "about 24 s left", then 100 % and "took 34 s") differ from each other in every byte. Tests ( tests/test_pi_view.py , 59 pass): the painter is a task and not a thread; a run's card paints about twice a second with no report and no press; a tick and a report never cost two frames in one half second; a thousand reports cost at most two frames; a finished run keeps its own words against a late tick; plus the paging rules (page math, replaced-not-appended lines, both ends unreachable by pressing, short last page never padded, one-page numbers have nowhere to turn). test_a_thousand_reports_cost_at_most_two_frames and the tick/report test are new for this change.

docs.text: What happened: the project notes were migrated out of Trilium notes into docs/ with a mkdocs.yml at the root. The whole set — plus the generated site/ output — was committed and pushed before being scrubbed . What it exposed: the Linux account name, carried in a Flet app id ( com.<personal>.anycalc and its .desktop file id), in an absolute home path ( /home/<user>/Android/Sdk ), in /dev/kvm ACL output, and in /tmp paths derived from the account name ( hsperfdata_<user> , <user>-code-zsh , android-<user> ). The same text existed twice : once in docs/ , again in the committed site/ HTML and in site/search/search_index.json , which flattens every page into one searchable blob. The undo: the leak was the tip commit, so git push --force-with-lease=main:<leaked SHA> took it off origin/main in one step. Verified afterwards: no forks, no PRs, no Pages site, no branch protection — and every blob of every commit reachable from the restored tip matches none of the PII patterns, so the published chain is clean. GitHub may keep serving the unreachable commit by SHA until it garbage-collects; that is the one part outside our control. The SHA is deliberately not quoted here. Scrub rule applied to the docs: current-state pages carry the real handle-based id ( com.github.greentruck50.anycalc ); change-log entries that describe the old id keep it neutral ( com.<personal> , <org>.anycalc.desktop , $HOME -relative paths, <user> placeholders) — substituting the new value into a historical sentence would make the sentence false. site/ is build output, not source: the staged copy is deleted and regenerated with .venv/bin/mkdocs build (mkdocs 1.6.1). Never hand-edit it, and treat it as a publishing surface — it mirrors every word of docs/ , so it carries the identical PII exposure. Spec: the pi section of calculator_spec.md now requires the half-second repaint on the page's own event loop, the schedule rather than chained sleeps, the one shared two-frames-a-second budget across clock and checkpoints, and the card belonging to the outcome once a run ends; and for the digits dialog it forbids growing the list while it is scrolled and requires the page buttons, the footline and the scrollbar gutter.

Views and dialogs receive what they need (page, controls, callbacks, or the app object) instead of reaching into an app closure, which is what let the closure-based single file become a class plus plain functions. The Flet import root — the rule that matters (stock convention since 2026-10-24) [tool.flet.app] path = "src" makes Flet treat **src/** as the artifact's import root . The packager is package_python_app() ( flet_cli/commands/build_base.py:2514 ), which shells out to dart run serious_python:main package <app dir> ; the result is staged to build/python-app/ (verified at build_base.py:2843 , passed on as SERIOUS_PYTHON_APP ). Inside it the modules sit side by side: main.pyc, calculate.pyc, keypad.pyc, conversions.pyc, styles.pyc, ui.pyc, config.pyc, … plus assets/conversions.yaml . That folder, not the project root, is what the runner puts on **sys.path** . So every module of the app imports its siblings by bare name — from ui import AnycalcApp , from config import … , import calculate . That is the stock Flet convention: flet create scaffolds src/main.py with no **src/__init__.py** and puts pythonpath = ["src"] in its pytest config, i.e. src/ is an import root, never a package. Each way of starting the app supplies that root itself: flet run / flet build from [tool.flet.app] path , python src/main.py from sys.path[0] , pytest from pythonpath = ["src"] in [tool.pytest.ini_options] . Pylance needs the equivalent — "python.analysis.extraPaths": ["src"] in .vscode/settings.json , otherwise all bare-name imports go red. No longer allowed : src. -prefixed imports, src/__init__.py , and any sys.path / sys.modules fix-up code. On 2026-10-24 the ensure_src_package() shim was deleted from main.py , the REPO_ROOT insert from tests/conftest.py , and the anycalc console script ( [project.scripts] anycalc = "src.main:run_app" ) from pyproject.toml ; [tool.setuptools] now declares packages = [] / py-modules = [] so a pip install only resolves dependencies rather than dropping loose main / ui / config modules into site-packages. Open conflict to remember: the AGENTS.md rule "Keep pyproject.toml updated (…, the _anycalc_ entry point …)" was written for the console script. The user chose the stock convention knowing the console script goes away; the Flet entry point ( [tool.flet.app] module = "main" ) is still declared. AGENTS.md has not been amended. Assets keep working because config.py builds CONVERSION_CONFIG_PATH from Path(__file__) , and the packager keeps assets/ next to the modules — subdirectories survive the copy, which is also why assets/conversions.yaml is where the app expects it. __pycache__ is excluded from the bundle by default. Historical note: before 2026-10-24 the tree used absolute src.<module> imports, which required a shim in main.py to register src as a package rooted at the flattened artifact directory, because that root has no src package. The shim worked but the layout was not what Flet scaffolds; it was removed rather than kept.
