docs.text: Running log entry and reference for the test suite added 2026-10-24. 2026-10-24 — % is a real percent key on the regular pad; the Length xfail is gone tests/test_calculator_engine.py grew from 56 to 96 tests and the % block is split by pad. Regular pad (percent): 50% → 0.5, 200+10% → 220, 200-10% → 180, 200*10% → 20, 200/10% → 2000, chaining on the running total ( 200+10%+5% → 231), and a % with nothing in front of it being dropped by the rewrite, so a lone % still evaluates to 0 rather than erroring ( 5+% is what errors: the rewrite leaves 5+ , so = reports "Invalid expression"). Scientific pad (modulo): unchanged — 9%2 → 1, 7%2.5 → 2, -7%2 → -1, 5%0 → "Invalid result". The rewrite that makes a postfix % parseable ( apply_percent_operators : 200+10% → 200+_percent(10) , also wrapping a closing bracket like sqrt(4)% or a name like pi% ) is tested directly, as is is_percent_call . tests/test_conversion_engine.py (75 → 82 tests): the LENGTH_DRIFT data and its xfail(strict=True) marker are deleted . The exactness sweep no longer exempts the Length group — every terminating-decimal pair in it must come out bit-for-bit. The parsec is excluded by name, with the reason in a comment: a parsec is 648000/π astronomical units, so its factor is not a rational number and no literal can be exact. tests/test_app.py (6 → 7 UI tests): test_regular_calculator_percent_key_and_sign_change types 200+10% on the regular pad and asserts the live answer preview reads 220 (percent, not modulo), then checks 5% → 0.05 and the ± behaviour; test_scientific_calculator_percent_key_is_modulo pins 9%2 → 1 , so both meanings of the same key are covered through the real UI. Full suite verified 2026-10-24: **flet test** → 185 passed in 339 s (7 UI + 96 calculator engine + 82 conversion engine), no xfail, no skips. Engine only: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -k engine → 178 passed in ~3 s. 2026-10-24 — pytest + flet test suite added (conversion engine + UI) pyproject.toml : the dev extra now installs flet[test]>=1.0.4 (pulls in pytest , pytest-asyncio and the screenshot libraries) plus explicit pytest / pytest-asyncio pins; added [tool.pytest.ini_options] with asyncio_mode = "auto" and testpaths = ["tests"] . Runtime dependencies unchanged. New tests/conftest.py — puts the repo root on sys.path so both kinds of tests can import src.main (safe since the app only runs under __main__ ). New tests/test_conversion_engine.py — pure-python tests, no app host: every unit pair inside a group is reachable, every terminating-decimal pair stays bit-exact, chain hops re-evaluate to the values printed ( _evaluate_conversion_formula is re-run per hop), formula-flip, same-unit pass-through and cross-group errors are pinned, plus ~40 published reference values (NIST/legal) and a 37-digit cubic-mile precision check. New tests/test_app.py — Flet integration tests through flet.testing : drawer navigation to Scientific Calculator and to conversion pages, the conversion page converting live as the value changes, clearing the value clearing result + chain quietly, keypad arithmetic and = flipping EXPRESSION → RESULT. At the time the Length group still used rounded literals ( meter -> inch was x * 39.37007874 , mile -> nautical mile x / 1.150779448 ), which was encoded as xfail(strict=True) naming the offending formulas. Superseded the same day: the exact anchors (inch = 25.4 mm, mile = 1609.344 m, nautical mile = 1852 m, light-year = 9460730472580800 m) are now in the YAML and the marker is removed — see the entry above. Docs: README.md gained a "Tests" section, calculator_spec.md gained a "Testing" section (what belongs in engine tests vs UI tests, key conventions, the tester limits below), and the pyproject.toml header comment documents the test command. 2026-10-24 — keypad keys % (regular pad) and ± (both pads) New tests/test_calculator_engine.py — pure-python tests for the expression engine rather than the conversion graph: what the % key evaluates to and the 21-case ± sign-change table, each case also asserted to be its own inverse. Named …_engine.py on purpose so -k engine picks it up together with test_conversion_engine.py . The _%_ half of that file was rewritten the same day when _%_ stopped being modulo on the regular pad. tests/test_app.py gained test_regular_calculator_percent_key_and_sign_change (taps key-% and key-± on the regular pad and reads the live answer preview), and the drawer test now also asserts key-± exists after switching to Scientific. Tester gotcha worth remembering: a keypad key that exists in both the scientific rows and the regular rows is found twice , because scientific mode renders the regular rows underneath its own — find_by_key("key-±") returned count 2 (the pad already had this problem with ( and ) ). The app now keeps every key on the pad exactly once, so key-<label> stays unique and a UI test can assert count == 1 again. How to run .venv/bin/flet test # everything (185 tests, ~5½ min) .venv/bin/flet test -k engine # both engine test files, ~3 s, no Flutter host .venv/bin/flet test -k app # the 7 UI tests, ~4-6 min (~35-60 s per test) flet test must run from the workspace root (it reads pyproject.toml , and [tool.flet.app] points it at src/main.py ). It accepts pytest flags only — positional test paths are rejected with a usage error, so select with -k ( -k percent_key runs the two percent UI tests plus the matching engine ones); anything after -- goes to pytest verbatim ( -- -s for print output). The pure tests also run under plain .venv/bin/python -m pytest -k engine . flet test needs a display for the app hosts it boots ( WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0 XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 ). The first UI run provisions/builds the Flutter test harness; later runs reuse it, but every UI test still boots a fresh app host — that host boot, not the assertions, is what makes the suite slow. flet test leaves a build/ tree behind ( flutter , python-app , site-packages ). docs.text: Project documentation for anycalc — the Flet calculator app at ~/Documents/anycalc . Working rules for this project live in the repo's AGENTS.md ; the machine-readable feature spec lives in calculator_spec.md . This note is the human-facing documentation hub — design decisions, architecture, and change log go here rather than in loose text files. Stack Python 3.14 (venv at .venv ); requires-python = ">=3.11" Declared in **pyproject.toml** at the workspace root — there is no requirements.txt anymore: dependencies = ["flet[cli,desktop]>=1.0.4", "PyYAML>=6.0.3"] , dev tooling in the optional dev extra. flet-desktop is an Flet extra , not a dependency: without it ft.run() pip-installs it silently on first launch. [cli] gives the flet run / flet build commands. [web] and [test] extras are deliberately excluded. PyYAML>=6.0.3 — parses the conversions config (imported as yaml ) Everything else the app imports is stdlib ( ast , asyncio , math , operator , collections , dataclasses , decimal , pathlib , typing ) Verified running on Flet 1.0.4 (the project venv), 1.0.5 (a clean install), and inside a Linux bundle that resolved 1.0.5 at build time File layout Path Purpose src/main.py The entire app (~1,700 lines): expression engine, conversion engine, UI; ends in def run_app() behind an if __name__ == "__main__": guard src/__init__.py Makes src an importable package so the anycalc console script resolves src.main:run_app src/assets/conversions.yaml Declarative unit-conversion groups, units, icons, formulas calculator_spec.md Feature spec (must stay in sync with the app) pyproject.toml Metadata, runtime deps, anycalc console script, setuptools config, and the [tool.flet] build config (entry point src/main.py ) README.md Setup / run / build commands build/ Generated by flet build (Flutter project + Linux artifact); not source Architecture of src/main.py Top-level, non-UI code: load_conversion_config() — reads/parses conversions.yaml , returns (unit_groups, conversions) ; raises clear errors on invalid YAML. Conversions have no id , only a name ; formulas is a dict keyed by number, so iterate .values() find_conversion_path() — graph search for a route between two units; two passes ( allow_reverse False then True) so fully-forward routes win. Returns the list of (formula, reversed) hops it chose _contains_conversion_input() / _evaluate_conversion_formula() — forward evaluation of a formula AST _invert_conversion_formula() — algebraically reverses MD formulas by walking the AST and returns the value ; UD formulas are never reversed _flip_conversion_formula() — same algebra, but builds the reversed formula as an AST and unparses it for display ( x / 100 → x * 100 , (x * 9/5) + 32 → (x - 32) * 5 / 9 ). Dividing by a fraction is rewritten as multiplying by its reciprocal so the output stays readable ConversionStep / ConversionOutcome — frozen dataclasses describing one applied hop (from/to unit ids, configured formula , applied_formula as actually used, formula type, used_backwards , value in, value out) and a whole conversion convert_units() — end-to-end conversion entry point; returns a ConversionOutcome , so the UI can show the chain of operations rather than only the answer format_conversion_value() — plain-text rendering of a converted value calculate() — the expression evaluator: parses with ast , evaluates node-by-node, Decimal arithmetic, trig helpers honoring deg/rad, named variables copy_to_clipboard() / make_copy_button(get_value) — shared clipboard helper and the small icon button factory; the getter is read at click time so a button can never copy a stale value UI code lives inside main(page: ft.Page) — drawer navigation, keypad rebuild, variable prompts, history rendering, and the inline conversion form. Conversions are live. There is no Convert button: run_conversion() runs on the value field's on_change and on both dropdowns' on_select . A non-numeric or empty value clears the result and the chain silently; only real failures set result_field.error . The chain cards sit under the result: one card per hop showing the unit transition and that hop's in → out values, with the formula hidden behind a per-card "View formula" toggle (a reversed hop shows its formula already flipped). The chain itself is not copyable. The calculators have a live answer. preview_answer() evaluates the current expression and refresh_preview() shows it as a small grey number under the display box ( preview_value inside preview_slot ), hiding it when the expression is empty, half-typed, already a number, an error, or a result already in the display. It is refreshed from every path that can change the expression or its meaning: update_display() , handle_display_change() , toggle_angle() , assign_variable() , set_mode() . promote_preview() runs on = : the grey number grows to the display size, turns white, slides up and fades over PREVIEW_MORPH_MS , then page.run_task(finish_preview_morph, token) resets the slot (the token ignores a stale timer, preview_morphing stops refresh_preview() from cancelling the animation). Packaging & build ( pyproject.toml ) The entry point is inside **src/** , declared twice on purpose: [tool.flet.app] path = "src" + module = "main" (used by flet run / flet build ) and [project.scripts] anycalc = "src.main:run_app" (installed by pip install -e . ). Setuptools side: packages = ["src"] , include-package-data = true , package-data = {src = ["assets/*.yaml"]} so the YAML travels with an installed distribution. flet build linux is run from the workspace root , not from src/ — [tool.flet.app] is what lets the CLI find src/main.py there. validate_entry_point() ( flet_cli/commands/build_base.py:992 ) fails with "main.py not found in the root of Flet app directory" if app.path / app.module are wrong; --module-name is the CLI override. The [tool.flet] keys that matter here: org , product (app id com.github.greentruck50.anycalc , product label), app.path , app.module , linux.categories . Others available: artifact , company , copyright , bundle_id , splash , boot_screen , template.* , plus per-platform tool.flet.linux.* / .android.* / .ios.* / .macos.* / .web.* . Verified 2026-10-23: flet build linux --no-rich-output --yes from the root took ~2.5 min. Artifact build/linux/ (132 MB): native GTK runner anycalc embedding CPython 1:1 via libpython3.14.so , app/ ( main.pyc , __init__.pyc , assets/conversions.yaml byte-identical to the source), site-packages/ installed from pyproject (flet 1.0.5 + flet-cli + flet-desktop + PyYAML), data/flutter_assets , share/applications/com.github.greentruck50.anycalc.desktop . build/flutter (439 MB) is the intermediate Flutter project. The app is compiled to **.pyc** by default in the bundle — pass --no-compile-app to keep readable sources. A bundle executes the configured module as **__main__** ( _sp_run_module_as_main() in the generated build/flutter/lib/python.dart ), so if __name__ == "__main__": run_app() fires there too; the same pattern works for flet run (which spawns python -u src/main.py ) and for the installed console script. Artifact smoke test: WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0 XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 ./build/linux/anycalc ran until timeout killed it (exit 124) with only a benign cursor-theme warning — no Python traceback. Build prerequisites on this machine: Flutter 3.44.8 (the version Flet 1.0.4 pins, from flet/version.py ) already present at the managed path ~/flutter/3.44.8 ; find_flutter_batch() prefers ~/flutter/<version> before falling back to PATH , so a manual Flutter install is only found if it is on PATH . cmake, ninja, pkg-config, gcc/g++ are installed; ~/.flet/cache/ holds the build template and python-build-standalone. .venv has no setuptools , so building this project ( pip wheel . , pip install -e . ) needs pip's build isolation — --no-build-isolation fails. Ordering: nothing is sorted, it is all file order Verified by reading the live drawer control tree. There is no sorted() call anywhere in src/main.py . Surface Current order Where that order comes from Drawer: Unit Conversions items Length, Time, Temperature, Data Order of the conversions: list in the YAML; the drawer loops for conversion in conversion_options , and conversion_options is that list verbatim Drawer: Calculators Regular, Scientific Hard-coded NavigationDrawerDestination literals in the drawer's control list From / To dropdowns e.g. Length: nm, μm, mm, cm, m, km, in, ft, yd, mi, nmi, AU, ly, pc, kpc, Mpc, Gpc, Tm Order of the group's units: list — deliberately SI small→large, then imperial, then astronomical; not alphabetical Chain cards Order the hops were applied outcome.steps Which formula wins a route YAML formulas: dict order BFS iterates conversion["formulas"].values() in file order History drawer Newest first reversed(history[-MAX_HISTORY_ITEMS:]) Variable picker x y z μ g m a v t d F E P p ρ r A V T q I U R f λ , then unused letters b c e h i j k l n o s u w Hand-written _NAMED_VARIABLE_OPTIONS + generated leftovers appended Two constraints to respect when reordering: A conversion's menu label must be **<unit group name> + " Conversion"** . open_conversion() resolves the group with conversion["name"].removesuffix(" Conversion") against conversion_groups_by_name ; mismatching names raise "No unit group is defined for …". Reordering is safe, renaming one side is not. The drawer is index-based. handle_drawer_change() : index < 2 → set_mode(index) , else open_conversion(conversion_options[index - 2]) . The 2 is the count of calculator destinations — if calculators are added, removed or grouped, that offset must change too (a flat [(destination, action)] list would remove the hazard). Note: the From/To dropdowns have no enable_search (only the variable picker does), which matters on Data (43 units) and Length (18). Gotchas learned the hard way Flet 1.0.4 Dropdown has no **on_change** — the selection event is on_select ( on_text_change is for the filter text). Handler names passed to a constructor are looked up when the control is built, so a nested handler must be defined above the control that uses it. A handler may, however, read a name assigned after the def (it is looked up when the handler runs) — that is how the chain cards let the toggle button relabel itself, and how the live run_conversion() reads controls defined below it. Flet 1.0 animation primitives: ft.AnimationStyle(duration=…, curve=ft.AnimationCurve.EASE_OUT_CUBIC) — the field is duration (an int is milliseconds), and Text / Container expose animate_size , animate_offset , animate_opacity , animate_scale plus on_animation_end . There is no ft.AnimationEasing and no colour animation, so a colour change during a morph snaps. Flet desktop client binaries are cached in ~/.flet/client/ (one dir per Flet version) and are prepared on first use of a new version — expect a pause after a version bump. Services ( ft.Clipboard ) self-register with the current page in Service.__post_init__ ; they are visible in the page's internal registry page._services._services , not in the page.services property list. Clipboard.get() returns a plain str | None , not an object with .data . A Flet app launched from a script prints its stdout through the CLI relay, which buffers; probes that need reliable output should write to a file, and must not rely on page.run_task(lambda: ...) — it requires a coroutine function ( page.run_task(async_fn, *args) works and is what the morph reset uses). src/main.py no longer ends in a bare ft.run(main) , so importing it (or src.main ) is safe for tests; the module-level guard only calls run_app() when executed as __main__ . Probes that exec the source still have to inject __file__ , because the conversion YAML path is derived from it. Probe text matching: a chain card's title and its value line both contain "→"; distinguish 1. Unit → Unit from 2500 → 25 before filtering. Parallel tool batches run concurrently — never pair a UI probe with reading its output file in the same batch. flet build needs a few seconds to unpack the build template and the standalone Python before any error appears, and the build dir build/ accumulates ~600 MB; a long-running flet build started from a tool batch must be backgrounded with its output redirected to a file. Verified limits & constants DECIMAL_PRECISION = 50 MAX_EXPONENT = 1000 MAX_EXPRESSION_LENGTH = 200 MAX_HISTORY_ITEMS = 20 Display / live preview: DISPLAY_TEXT_SIZE = 34 , DISPLAY_TEXT_COLOR = "#FFFFFF" , PREVIEW_TEXT_SIZE = 15 , PREVIEW_TEXT_COLOR = "#9CA3AF" , PREVIEW_MORPH_MS = 260 , PREVIEW_MORPH_LIFT = 34 (the display panel is 168 px tall to fit the preview line) Named variables x y z μ g m a v t d F E P p ρ r A V T q I U R f λ (each with a human description in the picker), plus additional generated options appended to VARIABLE_OPTIONS . Navigation ( ft.NavigationDrawer ) Opened from the header; two labelled sections separated by dividers: Calculators — Regular Calculator ( CALCULATE icon), Scientific Calculator ( SCIENCE icon) Unit Conversions — one destination per entry in the YAML conversions: list, icon resolved from the YAML icon field, label is the conversion's name Footer text: "Calculate anything." Selecting a destination swaps the main content area — conversions render inline there, never in a popup. Spec status calculator_spec.md currently specifies: Flet app, PEMDAS/BODMAS evaluation, YAML-driven conversions with forward-route preference and MD inversion, unit-ID integrity checks, the inline conversion form converting live (no Convert button, silent while typing), the conversion chain of operations (formula behind a "View formula" toggle), a "Live result preview" section for both calculators (grey live answer, promoted into the display on = ), the grouped drawer navigation, and copy-to-clipboard on the three result surfaces. 9. docs.text: Top-level, non-UI code: load_conversion_config() — reads/parses conversions.yaml , returns (unit_groups, conversions) ; raises clear errors on invalid YAML. Conversions have no id , only a name ; formulas is a dict keyed by number, so iterate .values() find_conversion_path() — graph search for a route between two units; two passes ( allow_reverse False then True) so fully-forward routes win. Returns the list of (formula, reversed) hops it chose _contains_conversion_input() / _evaluate_conversion_formula() — forward evaluation of a formula AST _invert_conversion_formula() — algebraically reverses MD formulas by walking the AST and returns the value ; UD formulas are never reversed _flip_conversion_formula() — same algebra, but builds the reversed formula as an AST and unparses it for display ( x / 100 → x * 100 , (x * 9/5) + 32 → (x - 32) * 5 / 9 ). Dividing by a fraction is rewritten as multiplying by its reciprocal so the output stays readable ConversionStep / ConversionOutcome — frozen dataclasses describing one applied hop (from/to unit ids, configured formula , applied_formula as actually used, formula type, used_backwards , value in, value out) and a whole conversion convert_units() — end-to-end conversion entry point; returns a ConversionOutcome , so the UI can show the chain of operations rather than only the answer format_conversion_value() — plain-text rendering of a converted value calculate() — the expression evaluator: parses with ast , evaluates node-by-node, Decimal arithmetic, trig helpers honoring deg/rad, named variables copy_to_clipboard() / make_copy_button(get_value) — shared clipboard helper and the small icon button factory; the getter is read at click time so a button can never copy a stale value UI code lives inside main(page: ft.Page) — drawer navigation, keypad rebuild, variable prompts, history rendering, and the inline conversion form. Conversions are live. There is no Convert button: run_conversion() runs on the value field's on_change and on both dropdowns' on_select . A non-numeric or empty value clears the result and the chain silently; only real failures set result_field.error . The chain cards sit under the result: one card per hop showing the unit transition and that hop's in → out values, with the formula hidden behind a per-card "View formula" toggle (a reversed hop shows its formula already flipped). The chain itself is not copyable. The calculators have a live answer. preview_answer() evaluates the current expression and refresh_preview() shows it as a small grey number under the display box ( preview_value inside preview_slot ), hiding it when the expression is empty, half-typed, already a number, an error, or a result already in the display. It is refreshed from every path that can change the expression or its meaning: update_display() , handle_display_change() , toggle_angle() , assign_variable() , set_mode() . promote_preview() runs on = : the grey number grows to the display size, turns white, slides up and fades over PREVIEW_MORPH_MS , then page.run_task(finish_preview_morph, token) resets the slot (the token ignores a stale timer, preview_morphing stops refresh_preview() from cancelling the animation).

docs.text: The entry point is inside **src/** , declared twice on purpose: [tool.flet.app] path = "src" + module = "main" (used by flet run / flet build ) and [project.scripts] anycalc = "src.main:run_app" (installed by pip install -e . ). Setuptools side: packages = ["src"] , include-package-data = true , package-data = {src = ["assets/*.yaml"]} so the YAML travels with an installed distribution. flet build linux is run from the workspace root , not from src/ — [tool.flet.app] is what lets the CLI find src/main.py there. validate_entry_point() ( flet_cli/commands/build_base.py:992 ) fails with "main.py not found in the root of Flet app directory" if app.path / app.module are wrong; --module-name is the CLI override. The [tool.flet] keys that matter here: org , product (app id com.github.greentruck50.anycalc , product label), app.path , app.module , linux.categories . Others available: artifact , company , copyright , bundle_id , splash , boot_screen , template.* , plus per-platform tool.flet.linux.* / .android.* / .ios.* / .macos.* / .web.* . Verified 2026-10-23: flet build linux --no-rich-output --yes from the root took ~2.5 min. Artifact build/linux/ (132 MB): native GTK runner anycalc embedding CPython 1:1 via libpython3.14.so , app/ ( main.pyc , __init__.pyc , assets/conversions.yaml byte-identical to the source), site-packages/ installed from pyproject (flet 1.0.5 + flet-cli + flet-desktop + PyYAML), data/flutter_assets , share/applications/com.github.greentruck50.anycalc.desktop . build/flutter (439 MB) is the intermediate Flutter project. The app is compiled to **.pyc** by default in the bundle — pass --no-compile-app to keep readable sources. A bundle executes the configured module as **__main__** ( _sp_run_module_as_main() in the generated build/flutter/lib/python.dart ), so if __name__ == "__main__": run_app() fires there too; the same pattern works for flet run (which spawns python -u src/main.py ) and for the installed console script. Artifact smoke test: WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0 XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 ./build/linux/anycalc ran until timeout killed it (exit 124) with only a benign cursor-theme warning — no Python traceback. Build prerequisites on this machine: Flutter 3.44.8 (the version Flet 1.0.4 pins, from flet/version.py ) already present at the managed path ~/flutter/3.44.8 ; find_flutter_batch() prefers ~/flutter/<version> before falling back to PATH , so a manual Flutter install is only found if it is on PATH . cmake, ninja, pkg-config, gcc/g++ are installed; ~/.flet/cache/ holds the build template and python-build-standalone. .venv has no setuptools , so building this project ( pip wheel . , pip install -e . ) needs pip's build isolation — --no-build-isolation fails.

docs.text: Flet 1.0.4 Dropdown has no **on_change** — the selection event is on_select ( on_text_change is for the filter text). Handler names passed to a constructor are looked up when the control is built, so a nested handler must be defined above the control that uses it. A handler may, however, read a name assigned after the def (it is looked up when the handler runs) — that is how the chain cards let the toggle button relabel itself, and how the live run_conversion() reads controls defined below it. Flet 1.0 animation primitives: ft.AnimationStyle(duration=…, curve=ft.AnimationCurve.EASE_OUT_CUBIC) — the field is duration (an int is milliseconds), and Text / Container expose animate_size , animate_offset , animate_opacity , animate_scale plus on_animation_end . There is no ft.AnimationEasing and no colour animation, so a colour change during a morph snaps. Flet desktop client binaries are cached in ~/.flet/client/ (one dir per Flet version) and are prepared on first use of a new version — expect a pause after a version bump. Services ( ft.Clipboard ) self-register with the current page in Service.__post_init__ ; they are visible in the page's internal registry page._services._services , not in the page.services property list. Clipboard.get() returns a plain str | None , not an object with .data . A Flet app launched from a script prints its stdout through the CLI relay, which buffers; probes that need reliable output should write to a file, and must not rely on page.run_task(lambda: ...) — it requires a coroutine function ( page.run_task(async_fn, *args) works and is what the morph reset uses). src/main.py no longer ends in a bare ft.run(main) , so importing it (or src.main ) is safe for tests; the module-level guard only calls run_app() when executed as __main__ . Probes that exec the source still have to inject __file__ , because the conversion YAML path is derived from it. Probe text matching: a chain card's title and its value line both contain "→"; distinguish 1. Unit → Unit from 2500 → 25 before filtering. Parallel tool batches run concurrently — never pair a UI probe with reading its output file in the same batch. flet build needs a few seconds to unpack the build template and the standalone Python before any error appears, and the build dir build/ accumulates ~600 MB; a long-running flet build started from a tool batch must be backgrounded with its output redirected to a file.
